I wanted to do a lil follow-up on the test capital I put into the @AxisFDN Origin Vault last month to test the deposit flow and see how the vault handled the position.

TL;DR: The 30-day lock ends this Friday, September 4, at 14:00 UTC, along with the Season 0 pre-deposit boost.

That means depositors can leave their position in the vault, redeem their ogUSDx into USDx, or move into another Season 1 position.

So here are the different options I'm considering:

→ Keep it in the Ecosystem Vault

This is the simplest option IMO because the vault moves to a flat 10x multiplier for Season 1 and is still the most hands-off way to stay in the ecosystem.

→ Redeem my $USDx

If I decide to take it out of the vault, I can either redeem for free over 7 days and keep earning Coordinates while it processes, or redeem instantly for roughly a 30 bps fee.

→ Hold $USDx

If I withdraw from the vault but want a higher multiplier without using an LP or Pendle position, holding USDx earns 16x Coordinates.

→ Use Axis’s market access to @CurveFinance

Providing liquidity in the $USDx / $USDT pool earns 20x Coordinates. I could provide liquidity rather than just hold $USDx, so there is a little more to consider.

→ Use Axis’s market access to @pendle_fi

Providing liquidity in the USDx Pendle market also earns 20x Coordinates.

Alternatively, YT-USDx earns the highest multiplier at 24x. It is also the highest-risk option because Pendle YT decays toward maturity and can go to zero.

Coordinates accrue daily based on your position and its multiplier. The same dollar only counts once, so multipliers don't stack.

So if you’re like me and deposited a small amount to test the vault, it’s worth reviewing the full Season 1 table before automatically swapping your USDx back into USDT.

Btw, you can find their full transparency dashboard here: https://t.co/y7WZTnpwez

What's your plan on this?

In 2022 there was a recurring problem: bootstrapping a new blockchain's liquidity was horrible.

It was almost impossible to get Uniswap or Curve to deploy, so the idea was simple: create a tiny, open-source, no-attribution scaffold that anyone could fork and deploy, even without technical ability.

Three contracts. Uniswap-style volatile liquidity. Curve-style stable liquidity. And a built-in ve flywheel to bootstrap and direct incentives.

So I created ve(3,3).

Since then, that design and its descendants have grown into:

• 163 unique app deployments
• 44 blockchains
• $748.8B in cumulative volume
• ~$16.0B in token(s) value

Although, to be fair, the data is heavily skewed: Aerodrome alone accounts for ~$424.2B of that volume, and Aerodrome today has evolved far beyond that original simple system.

What I find more interesting is how portable the idea became.

Robinhood Chain alone already has 18 different implementations/versions of the model.

The goal was never to build one DEX for every chain. It was to make the basic liquidity and incentive infrastructure simple enough that nobody had to wait for permission to have one.
